drug_class: CD38-directed monoclonal antibody combined with a hyaluronidase enzyme
purpose: This medicine is used to treat multiple myeloma, which is a type of blood cancer. It can be used alone or combined with other cancer medicines. It helps fight the cancer at different stages of the disease, including newly diagnosed and previously treated cases.
how_it_works: This medication contains a special protein called a monoclonal antibody that seeks out and attaches to a specific target called CD38, which is found on the surface of myeloma cancer cells. Once attached, it signals your immune system to find and destroy those cancer cells. The hyaluronidase ingredient helps the medicine spread and absorb under your skin more easily so it can be given as a quick shot instead of a long IV infusion.
common_side_effects: Common side effects include fatigue or tiredness, nausea, diarrhea, constipation, upper respiratory infections like a cold or stuffy nose, and low blood counts which can increase your risk of infections or bleeding. You may also notice injection site reactions like redness, swelling, or irritation where the shot is given.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious injection reactions, so your care team will monitor you closely during and after each dose. It can lower your white blood cells, red blood cells, and platelets, raising your risk of infections, anemia, and bleeding, so regular blood tests are important. It may also interfere with certain blood type tests, so always let any doctor or blood bank know you are taking this medicine. Tell your doctor right away if you develop fever, chills, trouble breathing, or signs of infection.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given as a shot under the skin, usually in the stomach area, by a healthcare professional in a clinic or hospital setting. The dosing schedule depends on what other medicines you are taking with it and what stage of treatment you are in — it may be given weekly, every two weeks, or every four weeks. Your doctor will create a personalized schedule that is right for your specific situation.
